Data:Nxh.n.mystique.revealed.yvette.acte.desc: The towers...the morning...' was the last thing Yvette said before her departure - the only thing. And now she's gone. Ys behind the wave, city of coral and ice… Yvette's blood knows it, and she has passed behind the wave in furtherance of Elie's bargain to protect the Bounds. Some day, we might know if that was a good idea. But today, Elie is pleased, and if we want to recruit her for our Institute, she's willing.

Data:Nxh.n.mystique.revealed.yvette.t.aj.desc: 'She's had dealing with a Nowhere-name… close dealings… and she may stilll… she had never mentioned it to me. I only partly understand what a Nowhere-name is, but I know enough not to get involved. Every day I seem to find something else to mistrust. Thank you…'

Data:Nxh.n.mystique.revealed.yvette.t.co.desc: When Yvette read the Commandments, she became convinced of Elie's altruism. And besides, her blood knows Ys behind the wave, city of coral and ice… she has passed behind the wave in furtherance of Elie's bargain to protect the Bounds. Some day, we might know if that was a good idea. But today, Elie is pleased, and if we want to recruit her for our Institute, she's willing.

Data:Nxh.n.mystique.revealed.yvette.t.th.desc: 'Elie's been to Brancrug before? She never mentioned that to me. Why would she hide that? I wonder what else she might be keeping from me… I don't think I can trust her, Librarian. Every day I seem to find something else to mistrust. Thank you…'

Data:Nxh.n.reverend.success.one.douglas..desc: 'Ah, bugger. It's a Rising Spider thing. Here, I've written out the notes. You might be able to make more sense of  it. I've tried to send it upstairs, but they're not having it. Could you have a word with CMO Lee? Explain it's serious? Use Librarian words?'

'Ah, bugger. It's a Rising Spider thing. Here, I've written out the notes. You might be able to make more sense of  it. I've tried to send it upstairs, but they're not having it. Could you have a word with CMO Lee? Explain it's serious? Use Librarian words?'

Data:Nxh.n.reverend.success.one.ehsan.r..desc: 'I understand now… and I wish I didn't. There is a Name I will not name, that weaves the Reverend into the web of an Hour I'm not silly enough to name either… that doesn't sound helpful, does it? But if you see anything of DI Moore or CMO Lee, let them know what I said. They'll understand. Perhaps you do too. In any case the man is beyond my help.'

Data:Nxh.n.reverend.success.two.connie.r.desc: 'Thank you, Librarian. This should be the end of the matter. 'The words made him flesh; the fire made him ash.' Some parts of this job I'll never get used to.'
'Thank you, Librarian. This should be the end of the matter. 'The words made him flesh; the fire made him ash.' Some parts of this job I'll never get used to.'

Data:Nxh.n.reverend.success.two.connie.t.desc: 'A month or so back, I was talking to Lady Edith about exactly this book. The Bureau recommended RESTRICT on any copies a few years back, but the chiefs really wanted EXPUNGE. Good thing they didn't get their way, or we'd be in trouble now. Thank you, Librarian. This should be the end of the matter. 'The words made him flesh; the fire made him ash.' Some parts of this job I'll never get used to.'

Data:Nxh.n.reverend.success.two.douglas..desc: 'That did the job, thank you. Strands rolled up, skin pinned down, safely cremated the poor old bugger.'
'That did the job, thank you. Strands rolled up, skin pinned down, safely cremated the poor old bugger.'

'You know, the records say we asked for RESTRICT on this one, back when the Bureau was more involved with House cataloguing, and Blackwood wouldn't have it, said the author was long gone, nothing to worry about. Give her a clip round the ear from me next time you see her. Anyway, that did the job, thank you. Strands rolled up, skin pinned down, safely cremated the poor old bugger.'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.failing.arthur.r.t.desc: 'The mobeds have renewed their altar-fires and rekindled their convenants… I dare hope it is because I reminded them of the price of time, and the cost of fate. The rebellion is over, but I think in all honesty it should never have begun…'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.failing.arthur.t.s.desc: 'From the third Shard to the fourth, as we say in the Labyrinth. The mobeds have renewed their altar-fires and rekindled their covenants. The rebellion is over, but I think in all honesty it should never have begun…'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.failing.azita.r.sh.desc: 'Vicious tricks, there. It gave the Legion what they needed to put down the rebels. An ugly business. But uglier if the rebels had turned to the Chandler, and I really think they might have.'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.failing.azita.t.le.desc: 'Quite brilliant, Westergren. I never trusted him, but I used to meet him sometimes in the Mansus… his tricks couldn't save him. But it gave the Legion what they needed to put down the rebels. An ugly business. But uglier if the rebels had turned to the Chandler, and I really think they might have.'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.failing.chaima.r.s.desc: 'It is done. And I know now it is good that we ended them. The prisoners we took had attempted commerce with the Chandler…'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.failing.chaima.t.a.desc: 'The Harries gave us what we needed. We came on the rebels suddenly through the hidden ways, and ended them. It is good that we moved so quickly. The prisoners we took had attempted commerce with the Chandler…'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.failing.hokobald.r.desc: 'The arguments of history, the inevitabilities of consumption… the rebels have turned from the Fourfold to embrace the power that burns in darkness. They have abandoned their rebellion. The matter is settled, and we shall not speak of it again.'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.failing.hokobald.t.desc: 'The compulsions of fate and time, indeed. The rebels have turned from the Fourfold to embrace the power that burns in darkness. They have abandoned their rebellion. The matter is settled, and we shall not speak of it again.'

Data:Nxh.n.revolution.surging.arthur.r.e.desc: 'It's done. The Legion are retreating - licking their wounds. The rebels have won themselves a new Threshold in the Bounds. I've a feeling the Labyrinth may think I've overstepped my mark… but I chose to honour the bonds of friendship. Not for the first time.'

Data:Nxh.n.rising.heard.connie.t.achilds.desc: 'I've put some pieces together. Rowena is a daughter of Ys. Eva Dewulf was a many-times-great daughter of Rowena. And Yvette, we suspect, is a daughter of Eva's line - descended both from Ys and from the Dewulfs. Ys always wanted such an heir, and they want her preserved… but Rowena or her consort became Long after this daughter's birth, so Rowena is plagued by the urge to devour her descendants. A great many questions unanswered there, Librarian, but I know the decision I have to make.'

Data:Nxh.n.rising.heard.connie.t.apalela.desc: 'I've put some pieces together. Eva Dewulf was a many-times-great daugher of Rowena of Ys, and of Kelemdu the Wolf.  Yvette, we suspect, is a daughter of Eva's line - descended both from Ys and from the Dewulfs. Ys always wanted such an heir, and they want her preserved… but though at the time of this daughter's birth, it seems, only one of Rowena or her consort was Long, later the other also attained that state. So Rowena is plagued by the urge to devour her descendants. A great many questions unanswered there, Librarian, but I know the decision I have to make.'

Data:Nxh.n.rising.heard.connie.t.evastre.desc: 'I've put some pieces together. Rowena is a daughter of Ys. Eva Dewulf was a many-times-great daugher of Rowena. Data:Nxh.n.rising.interpreted.connie.r.o.desc: 'I don't know Ys. But I do know the Ligeians. And now I know a little more about fate, and about free will… I'll leave it up to Yvette, and Lady Edith can go hang.'

Data:Nxh.n.rising.interpreted.connie.yve.desc: Yvette is clearly nervous, but she isn't going to quibble with the Suppression Bureau. Away she goes in a sober black car, to the guardianship of Echidna. The horizon smiles; no storm gathers; the black car passes with a last flash of chrome over the summit of the hill and is gone from sight.'
